incident-bot: [ALERT] 2026-03-15T02:01:07Z - P1 - node gpu-a-7 experiencing repeated container restarts and CUDA failures during high-paged-attention load. Multiple ri-infer pods crashed with OOMs. Observed error spikes on /v1/generate and increased 5xx rate.

maria (oncall): ack. i'm investigating, paging eng-runtime. locking the thread for incident coordination.

raj (eng-oncall): i'm pulling logs from gpu-a-7 now. tailing /var/log/containers/ri-infer*.log
```
[2026-03-15T01:59:58Z] ri-infer-12 Restarting container (OOMKilled)
[2026-03-15T02:00:05Z] cuda: cudaErrorLaunchOutOfMemory when launching attention kernel
[2026-03-15T02:00:10Z] allocator: paged-slab high-water 92%
kv_cache: resident=1.9GiB fragmentation=74% leak_rate=+3.4MiB/min
threadpool: stall detected, enqueue=312
```

jordan (eng-runtime): that looks like kv cache fragmentation + paged-attn allocator drift. repeated small allocs causing slab fragmentation, slow memory creep into OOM. probable trigger: long-context batched requests + prefix caching.

maria (oncall): initial mitigations: 1) throttle /v1/generate to 30rps; 2) disable large-batch (batch_size>8) for affected pool; 3) route heavy customers to fallback small-quant model. doing now.

raj (eng-oncall): running cordon/drain on ri-infer-12 to force restart and trigger warm-up on other nodes.
```bash
kubectl cordon node/gpu-a-7
kubectl drain node/gpu-a-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

deploy-bot: rolling restart triggered for deployment ri-infer-pool-a by raj at 2026-03-15T02:05:03Z.

sre-bot: snapshot metrics attached: mem.used_paged=86%, kv.fragmentation=0.74, cuda.err.rate=0.18

jordan (eng-runtime): short term workaround: reduce kv cache target from 8Gi to 4Gi (config change) to force more aggressive eviction and free up compactable pages. We'll also temporarily set attention paging threshold lower so fewer pages are pinned. Preparing hotpatch.

maria (oncall): applying configmap change for inference.runtime.kv_target=4Gi and patching model routing to fallback. do we want to also disable prefix caching for enterprise routes?

jordan (eng-runtime): yes disable prefix caching for any request > 1024 tokens for 20m. also set allocator debug=1 to get page compaction traces.

raj (eng-oncall): applied configmap change; restarting pods to pick up config. monitoring fragmentation metric now.

keiko (cs): customer impact - two Dedicated customers reported ~15-25% request failures between 01:58-02:07 UTC. enterprise alerts triggered. i've sent initial notifications: "we're mitigating memory fragmentation, temporary rate limits and fallbacks in place, ETA 20m for stabilization". No data loss or security impact reported.

jordan (eng-runtime): after restarts, fragmentation metric fell from 74% -> 59% within 3 minutes. CUDA OOM error rate almost zero on restarted pods. However one node shows repeated small increases; suspect slow leak in paged allocator for long-lived kv slots. Need a follow-up patch to force compaction every N evictions.

maria (oncall): good. keep an eye on tail latency; customers on Hosted may still see elevated 4xx/5xx for long contexts. rollback plan: if errors increase we revert kv_target to 8Gi and put stricter rate limit (20 rps) and small-quant fallback.

raj (eng-oncall): collecting heap/profile from a running pod for analysis. command: 
```bash
kubectl exec -it ri-infer-xx-5 -- /usr/local/bin/dump-kv-state --out /tmp/kvstate.pb && kubectl cp ri-infer-xx-5:/tmp/kvstate.pb ./kvstate-5391234567.pb
```

jordan (eng-runtime): please upload the pb to the secure incident bucket (s3://ri-incidents/paged-kv/5391234567) and mark as sensitive. I'll run offline compaction sim.

keiko (cs): updated customers with timeline. one asked for ETA 1h if stabilization lingers; asked to be prioritized for Dedicated remediation.

maria (oncall): summary & next steps for handoff:
- Cause: suspected paged-attention allocator fragmentation + slow kv cache leak under long-context batching -> OOMs and node flaps.
- Actions taken: throttled /v1/generate, disabled large-batch, routed heavy customers to fallback model, cordoned & drained affected node, reduced kv_target to 4Gi, restarted pods, collecting kv state and profiles.
- Current status: fragmentation dropped to ~59%, cuda OOMs resolved on restarted pods, overall 5xx rate returning to baseline but some dedicated tenants still impacted.
- Open items: upload profile, engineer hotfix to force compaction on eviction, longer-term mitigations (allocator patch + eviction tuning), post-incident rollout plan.

maria (oncall): handing off to night oncall tony at 2026-03-15T02:15:00Z (tony is covering after me). please watch the leak_rate metric (kv.leak_rate) and fragmentation. if fragmentation creeps above 70% or OOMs return, escalate to eng-runtime and consider emergency capacity shift to spare pool.

tony (oncall-next): acked. i'll take it from here, have the runbook open. will push for hotfix PR from eng-runtime owners and coordinate next customer update.

incident-bot: next-update in 20 minutes or on material change. tags: paged-attention, kv-cache, node-flap, cuda-oom, oncall-handoff
